newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Stals sanguine on S.Africa BOP, rand despite gold.
newsitem.headline: Stals sanguine on S.Africa BOP, rand despite gold.

text.p: South African Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals believes the recent fall in the gold price should not create any undue problems for the country's balance of payments or the rand.
Gold's fall to a 12-year low this month had created nervousness in the financial markets, Business Report newspaper on Thursday quoted him telling an Institute of Directors lunch.

"Its effect on the balance of payments, however, should be judged against a total level of exports of goods and services that now exceeds 150 billion rand a year, with gold contributing less than 18 percent of the total," he said.

"Total capital inflow through the bond market and stock exchange was double the value of gold production in the first six months of 1997. Should the present price of $320 (an ounce) be maintained for a full year, the loss in foreign exchange on the balance of payments will amount to 4.5 billion rand, or less than three percent of total exports."
That amount should not create any undue pressue on the rand exchange rate, he said.
